findings.priority_reason: Changes how Zsh completion items containing colons are formatted, affecting how the shell interprets and displays these completions.
findings.title: Escape colons in Zsh completion values
findings.before: Completion values containing colons were returned as-is to the Zsh shell, which sometimes caused issues with Zsh's _describe function.
findings.after: Completion values now have their colons escaped (represented as \:) unless the item lacks a help string, ensuring better compatibility with Zsh completion processing.
findings.scenario: A completion item contains a colon in its value (e.g., file path or specific flag format).
findings.potential_impact: Users relying on Zsh completion may see colons rendered correctly in their shell rather than interpreted as delimiter markers by Zsh's internal completion logic.
findings.review_question: Does escaping colons in Zsh completion values resolve the identified compatibility issues with _describe without breaking existing shell parsing logic for items without help text?

example.input: A completion item contains a colon in its value (e.g., file path or specific flag format).
